points: After 430 silent days, Yechezkel suddenly speaks to the elders of Yehudah and is carried by his hair to Yerushalayim. The Radak says this third vision relates to the final galus, under Tzidkiyahu.
Avodah zarah destroyed the Beis HaMikdash. Yechezkel sees four scenes there: the semel hakinah, the elders led by the head of the Sanhedrin, women serving Tammuz, and men bowing to the sun.

The Malbim says the semel hakinah resembles Zoroastrianism, appeasing a force of evil. The men with their backs to the Beis HaMikdash were serving Baal Peor, worshipping by defecating before the idol.
Since Yoshiyahu there was no real idolatry in the Beis HaMikdash. The Malbim says some trace remained. Hashem punishes us for our ancestors' flaws if we don't fix them, and we are best placed to.

Believing evil exists apart from Hashem, or that part of us is truly evil, is still idolatry. So is Baal Peor's cynicism that nothing is sacred. Until we uproot these, we can't expect the Beis HaMikdash.
